title: 2.1.14 Guard with a Truthy Check
description: Write an if statement that tests a variable directly, relying on truthy/falsy conversion. Auto-graded.

steps.title: Declare a string variable
steps.instructions: Create a variable called searchTerm and set it to an empty string "".

steps.title: Test it directly
steps.instructions: Write an if statement whose condition is just searchTerm (no comparison operator). Log a message for when it's truthy, and add an else that logs a message for when it's falsy.

requirements.title: if statement tests searchTerm directly and logs
requirements.description: if statement condition is a bare searchTerm with no comparison operator, and logs inside the block. Help: 2.1.12 (Truthy and Falsy Values)

requirements.title: else branch logs
requirements.description: Code contains an else branch that calls console.log. Help: 2.1.12 (Truthy and Falsy Values)

aiCheck.rubricTitle: What the AI read in your code
aiCheck.prompt: The student wrote JavaScript for the lab "2.1.14 Guard with a Truthy Check". The task they were given: Create a variable called searchTerm and set it to an empty string "". You cannot run their code: read it and judge what it WOULD do. Judge each criterion by whether the idea is achieved, however the student wrote it. Different variable and function names, template strings, arrow functions, semicolons, spacing, quotes and order are all fine. Do not require any particular structure unless the criterion names one. Mark a criterion missing only when the idea is absent or the code does the opposite. Code inside a comment never runs. Write each note for THIS student's own code: in a not-met note, name the exact line or name in their code that causes the problem (quote at most a few words of it), say in plain words what it does now versus what the criterion needs, and give one concrete next thing to try, but do NOT write the corrected code. In a met note, say in one short phrase what in their code satisfied it. Do not use generic praise.
